narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. The architecture has three layers. Observe (Layer 1): lightweight desktop sensors capture work patterns including application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation. Intelligence Layer (Layer 2): a "Brain" that detects employee intent, the business value of tasks, and "drift" where work diverges from the intended flow. Execution Layer (Layer 3): an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates. The system uses existing foundation models rather than building its own LLMs, focusing instead on the "Work Graph" to reveal where resources are burned and where AI can intercept work mid-flow to provide assistance. Vision: a single system that observes how work happens, decides what AI should do next, and auto-builds agents continuously to ensure a "Continuous AI lift."

raw.thesis:
Narma is creating an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" to help AI-first companies implement AI automation effectively and at scale. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: observing work patterns with desktop sensors (Layer 1), an Intelligence Layer that understands employee intent and business value (Layer 2), and an Execution Layer that automatically generates and deploys AI agents (Layer 3). This system doesn't build new foundational AI models but instead leverages existing ones, focusing on understanding the "Work Graph" — how work actually flows within an organization. This allows Narma to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for AI intervention, ultimately aiming for "Continuous AI lift."

The venture is for AI-first companies, specifically those struggling with quantifying AI benefits, measuring ROI, and managing system and human resource "drift." The problem it addresses is significant: enterprises currently lack the necessary telemetry to identify AI savings, struggle with unreliable ROI metrics, and face constant divergence in operational processes. Narma seeks to provide a comprehensive solution that observes work, decides on AI next steps, and continuously builds agents.

The founder's goal, while not explicitly stated, appears to be a growth startup, given the ambition to provide "Continuous AI lift" and target AI-first companies. The venture is currently at the idea stage, as indicated by the detailed architectural description without mention of a working prototype or deployed system. Narma is positioned to replace disparate, manual methods of identifying AI opportunities and measuring their impact with an integrated, automated system. It also complements existing AI models by providing the orchestration layer for their deployment and ongoing optimization.
